experiment: extraction averaging judged on 233 subjects never used in training
the_hard_limitation: the published Ooi features exist only for the 753, so the in-fold winner A+C (0.7440) CANNOT be scored on new subjects. This test uses the two arms whose features exist outside the 753: our own 400 (B) and the 450 re-extraction (C).
protocol: train once on 728, predict 233 holdout; g=0.92, w=0.05, filter keep 150, lambda by in-fold CV on the training block
finding: FOR THE FIRST TIME THE EXTRACTION AVERAGE TRANSFERS. B+C reaches 0.7827 against 0.7795 for the best single arm on subjects the models never saw. The parallel session's F and G failed this test twice.
honest_read: +0.0032 with a bootstrap interval that includes zero. Real in direction, not decisive in size. The qualitative claim it supports is the important one: averaging two extractions costs nothing on new subjects and may gain.
